content: I’ll first read the workspace contract and inventory the current rollout evidence. Then I’ll use the required fish-control bookshelf protocol and the wake-visual inspection skill before changing the single policy candidate.

I’m using two workspace skills: `fish-control-primitives` because the protocol requires a fresh mechanism-level consultation, and `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because trajectory metrics alone cannot distinguish route error from wake-induced loss of authority. I’ll follow their evidence-routing instructions before proposing the architecture.

The assigned evidence is unusually consistent: all four sampled solver summaries report the same successful arrival (`137.357` release units), so the useful comparison will be that replicated best finite policy against an inherited failure/slow-success lineage. I’m checking whether the policies, metrics, and keyframes are truly duplicates before treating replication as independent causal evidence.

The visual contrast is now clear. The replicated best policy makes one broad targetward arc, then enters the inter-row wake while continuing upstream and capturing. The inherited `left_domain` case also reaches the wake and gets as close as `1.796L`, but its path repeatedly folds, turns away from the target, and ultimately exits the top boundary. I’m tracing the exact one-mechanism policy differences and load signals before selecting a transferable primitive.

The wake evidence points away from more gain or more independent residuals: the failure reaches `31.416 rad/time²` on joint 1, doubles energy, and loses route topology despite only modestly higher RMS moment. Following the bookshelf protocol, I’m now consulting compact mechanisms that preserve the successful oscillator while conditioning route authority on physically meaningful feedback.

The shelf consultation supports one compact transfer: turning should arise from curvature asymmetry across the traveling bend, not from simply amplifying both joints on the same half-cycle. That distinction matches the inherited evidence—same-sign posterior amplification produced large loops—so I’ll test a small opposite posterior modulation while leaving target bearing, progress qualification, direct moment feedback, oscillator, and base tail lag intact. First I’m recording the pre-edit diagnosis and falsification criteria as required.

The candidate now preserves every evidenced successful loop and changes only the cross-joint curvature distribution: an 8% bounded opposite posterior modulation replaces the failed same-sign intuition. I’m updating durable guidance with the inherited negative results; I will not claim this unevaluated candidate as evidence.
I’m invoking the workspace check-runner now. Its checks are static only: guidance provenance, the two-joint policy contract, and the editable-file boundary; no CFD rollout will be run.

The guidance check passed. The contract command itself could not start because this runner image has no `julia` on `PATH`; I’m checking the workspace/toolchain locations and will rerun the same non-CFD contract if a local Julia binary is available.
